title: Charge-Sector Construction of the Type-IIB Axion--Dilaton Wormhole Partition Function
abstract: I construct the Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole partition function from charge-sector data. In a chosen axion charge, equivalently form-field flux sector, the long-distance saddle calculation supplies a two-end operator term with coefficient matrix \(C^{ij}_ν\). The labels \(i,j\) label end-insertion operators; the labels \(A,B\) label parent universes. Reduction data \(b\) convert this matrix into scalar coefficients \(W_ν[b]\). The wormhole partition function in the theta variable is \(Z_{\rm wh}(θ;b)=\sum_νW_ν[b]\e^{iνθ}\). I analyze properties and constraints this coefficients satisfy: discrete-symmetry covariance, phase, absolute bounds, moment positivity, Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities for the unreduced coefficient matrix, complex-\(θ\) domains, charge-lattice tails, and the dilute Bessel/Skellam limit. The \(θ\)-dependence of the wormhole partition function is the Fourier transform of the charge-sector scalar coefficients.
summary: This paper constructs the partition function for a Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole using a charge-sector expansion. It analyzes this function by deriving constraints on its coefficients, showing how imposing physical requirements—such as positivity or symmetry—imposes deep mathematical structure on the resulting theta series.
main_problem: The primary goal is constructing the Type-IIB axion--dilaton wormhole partition function, Z_wh(theta; b), by systematically analyzing its dependence on charge-sector data.
main_result: The paper establishes a hierarchy of mathematical constraints—including discrete symmetry covariance, moment positivity, and Cauchy–Schwarz inequalities—that the coefficients of this theta expansion must satisfy depending on the physical assumptions made.
method: The method involves deriving the partition function through a multi-step process: calculating an initial coefficient matrix from semiclassical saddle points in each charge sector, followed by a reduction operation using specific data (b) to yield scalar coefficients W_nu[b].
model_or_system: The model is Type-IIB string theory compactification involving wormhole geometries. The analysis focuses on the resulting partition function expressed as a Fourier series in the variable theta, conjugate to an integer axion charge.
key_observables: The wormhole partition function Z_wh(theta; b), the reduced scalar coefficients W_nu[b], and the absolute bound Z_abs[b].
important_parameters: The compact Fourier variable theta, the integer charge index nu, and the reduction data vector b.
main_assumptions: Assumptions range from assuming positive reduced coefficients (leading to moment positivity) to assuming the unreduced coefficient matrix forms a positive quadratic form. The final microscopic calculation of the coefficients remains an external task.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates geometric objects related to the wormhole throat and two-end operators. Figure 2 summarizes the mathematical flow: Saddle Calculation -> Coefficient Matrix C_ij^nu -> Reduction R_b -> Scalar Coefficients W_nu[b] -> Partition Function Z_wh(theta; b).
paper_structure: The paper follows a logical progression from defining the physical object (wormhole partition function) to deriving its mathematical structure via charge-sector expansion, and finally analyzing this structure by imposing increasingly stringent physical constraints (symmetry, positivity, etc.) on the resulting coefficients.
why_interesting: While highly theoretical, the rigorous development of coefficient constraints based on physical assumptions (like positivity leading to moment functions) mirrors techniques used in quantum field theory and statistical mechanics for ensuring physical consistency.
